orientation: PR-1 implements customer onboarding and KYC compliance verification. It introduces domain models, event definitions, an application service for customer registration and verification/rejection, account opening enforcement rules, and controller endpoints. The goal is to allow customers to submit personal identity details while preventing underage applicants or unverified customers from opening bank accounts.

findings.title: Class-level Customer policy prevents compliance officers from verifying or rejecting registrations
findings.claim: In ASP.NET Core, Authorize attributes combine cumulatively across controller and action levels. Because [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] is declared on the CustomersController class, Verify and Reject require callers to satisfy both Customer and Compliance policies simultaneously, blocking compliance officers who do not hold customer credentials.
findings.requirement_link: HTTP endpoints are exposed with [ApiController] and explicit [Authorize(Policy = ...)] attributes: POST api/customers (Customer policy, derives user id solely from ICurrentUser), GET api/customers/me (Customer policy, returns current user's customer), POST api/customers/{id}/verify (Compliance policy), and POST api/customers/{id}/reject (Compliance policy).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the CustomersController class declaration so that each action's method-level [Authorize] attribute controls access independently.

findings.claim: In ASP.NET Core, class-level and action-level [Authorize] attributes are combined with logical AND. Specifying [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on CustomersController forces callers of Verify and Reject to satisfy both Policies.Customer and Policies.Compliance, causing HTTP 403 Forbidden for compliance officers who do not possess the Customer role.

findings.title: Redundant and conflicting controller-level Authorize attribute
findings.claim: Applying [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level causes ASP.NET Core to evaluate it conjunctively for every action in the controller. This makes lines 27 and 46 redundant and inadvertently forces Verify and Reject (lines 56 and 79) to require both Customer and Compliance policies, risking authorization failures for compliance officers.
findings.requirement_link: HTTP endpoints are exposed with [ApiController] and explicit [Authorize(Policy = ...)] attributes: POST api/customers (Customer policy, derives user id solely from ICurrentUser), GET api/customers/me (Customer policy, returns current user's customer), POST api/customers/{id}/verify (Compliance policy), and POST api/customers/{id}/reject (Compliance policy).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the CustomersController class declaration so that each action exclusively enforces its own explicit Authorize policy.

findings.title: CustomersController endpoints lack unit or integration tests
findings.claim: The newly introduced CustomersController and its four endpoints (Register, Me, Verify, Reject) have no unit or integration tests. Routing, HTTP status code mapping (200, 400, 403, 404, 409), and policy authorization attributes ([Authorize(Policy = ...)]) are entirely unexercised by the test suite.

findings.suggested_fix: Add controller tests verifying endpoint execution, status code translation for exceptions (BadRequest, Forbid, NotFound, Conflict), and authorization policy metadata.

dropped_findings.title: Variable minDob is misleadingly named for maximum allowable birth date
dropped_findings.claim: The variable minDob represents the latest (maximum) birth date permitted for an applicant to be at least 18 years old. Naming a chronological cutoff date 'minDob' when values greater than it are rejected is inverted and confusing for future maintainers.
dropped_findings.requirement_link: all timestamps and age checks use IClock.UtcNow rather than DateTime.Now or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.
dropped_findings.suggested_fix: Rename minDob to maxDob or latestAllowedDob to reflect that it is the upper bound on date of birth.
anchor: throw new ArgumentException("Applicant must be at least 18 years old.", nameof(request));
